subject: POC capacity planning - reserved GPUs & autoscale plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Liang <ben@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning - reserved GPUs & autoscale plan

Hi Ben / Sasha,

Great to meet yesterday - thanks for the time and the demo context. Per our call I wanted to capture the proposed POC eval plan and the capacity/ops details so we can align on success criteria and who owns each item. High level: 2-week POC to validate latency and cost at ~5k QPS-equivalent requests (chat + embeddings mix).

Success criteria (what Acme has asked to validate):
- Avg 95th percentile latency < 350 ms for text generation at target traffic profile
- Throughput of sustained 150 concurrent sessions (chat-like usage) without queueing
- Token cost target <= $0.002/token (goal to compare against internal baseline)
- No data leakage; all logs retained per your retention policy (30 days)

POC plan & timelines:
- Week 0: Kickoff + baseline run (track current latencies) - owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Sasha (Acme)
- Week 1: Reserved GPUs provisioned + load test ramp to 50% - owner: Dev (Redwood) ops + Acme infra
- Week 2: Autoscale policy enabled, burst tests to peak expected (x3 baseline) - owner: Dev (Redwood) ops
- End of Week 2: Joint run and evaluation; decision: go/no-go for reserved capacity pilot

Capacity proposal (initial):
- Reserved pool for POC: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (single-tenant reserved pool)
- Autoscale: allowed burst up to +4 GPUs (total potential 8) for short bursts (10-30 minutes) - cool-down 15m
- Expected steady-state concurrency headroom covers your 150 concurrent sessions; burst handles peak traffic during demo windows

Operational notes:
- Prefix/KV caching will be enabled for repeated prompts to reduce token cost during evaluation
- We'll provide a small sample load harness and telemetry dashboard (token counts, per-route latency, GPU utl)

Attachments: ACME_POC_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (detailed numbers, instance types, autoscale rules) and redwood-poc-terms-draft.pdf (standard POC terms).

Next steps / asks for Acme:
1) Confirm the success criteria above or send edits by EOD Friday
2) Confirm we can schedule a 1-hour kickoff next Tuesday (09/15) with your infra and SRE
3) Provide a contact for VPN/ingress and (optional) KMS key if you want encrypted persistence during POC

Happy to adjust the reserved sizes depending on your internal baseline metrics - if you have a sample workload report we can fine tune.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful and aligns closely with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: the latency target is fine but can we add an availability target for the POC (>= 99.5% overall during run window)?
- For cost comparison, we'll measure end-to-end token spend across the 2 weeks; confirm you'll provide per-route token breakdowns
- Reserved pool: 4 x A100 sounds OK for week 1. For the burst policy we want to ensure we can reach up to 10 GPUs for up to 5 minutes for load tests - our e2e demo generates spikes when multiple teams run tests concurrently. Is that feasible or a hard limit at 8?

Also, quick ask: can we get the telemetry dashboard and a sample load harness this week so our infra team can prep ingress rules?

Ben

Hi Ben - thanks for the quick reply and the three asks. Quick responses inline below and an updated plan attached.

- Availability: yes - we can target >= 99.5% for the POC run window. We will instrument health checks and synthetic pings to measure availability and report daily.
- Per-route token breakdowns: confirmed - dashboard will include token counts by route + per-request latency. We'll hand over the dashboard link and exportable CSVs after kickoff.
- Burst limit: we can extend the burst ceiling to 10 GPUs for short windows (<= 5 minutes) for the load test, but will need a short pre-approved allowance so our pool scheduler can allocate. That means for the POC we'll set burst max = 10 GPUs, with a max concurrent burst time of 5m and a 20m cooldown. If spikes exceed that we'll fall back to queued requests - we'll capture the behavior in the run.

Updated capacity plan (attached):
- Reserved: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Burst: up to +6 GPUs (total 10) for up to 5 minutes (approved for load tests)
- Autoscale policy: enable after 30% CPU/GPU sustained for 3m; scale step +2 GPUs; max 10 for POC

Operational items we'll own:
- Redwood: provision reserved pool, configure autoscale policy, provide dashboard and load harness, daily checkpoint emails
- Acme: provide ingress rules, KMS/key access if needed, run your end-to-end test harness and share baseline workload by Monday morning

Next steps:
1) I'll send calendar invites for kickoff Tue 09/15 10am PT (30-60m) - Dev will join for provisioning
2) Please upload any baseline workload or traffic profile to the Drive folder (link below) by Monday EOD
3) We'll provision reserved GPUs within 24-36 hours after kickoff (assuming no procurement blockers)

Links / attachments: ACME_POC_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (attached) and Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmePOC
